svg.title: Paris Peace Accords (1973), NVA Spring Offensive & The Fall of Saigon (1972–75)
svg.desc: Deterministic 1:10m Natural Earth GIS atlas map of Indochina (1972–1975) charting Operation Linebacker II over Hanoi and Haiphong (Dec 1972), the January 1973 Paris Peace Accords ceasefire-in-place leaving ~150,000 NVA troops in South Vietnam, General Van Tien Dung's March–April 1975 NVA Spring Offensive from Ban Me Thuot, Huế, and Da Nang through Xuan Loc, and Operation Frequent Wind during the Fall of Saigon on 30 April 1975.

text.tspan: Paris Ceasefire • ~150,000 NVA Stay in South
④ Huế & Da Nang Collapse (25–29 Mar)
Chaotic ARVN Northern Rout in Days
Op. Frequent Wind Airlift → NVA Seize Palace

g.text: KEY • PEACE ACCORDS & FALL OF SAIGON (1972–75)
US B-52 'Christmas Bombings' force Jan 1973 Accords
~150,000 NVA troops remain inside South as US exits
Armoured thrusts: Ban Me Thuot & Da Nang → Saigon
US helicopter evacuation from Saigon → US 7th Fleet
DRV & RVN Reunify as Socialist Vietnam (1976)
Cambodia & Laos also turn communist in 1975

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · PAPER 3 (OPTION 33) · KT4.3–4.4: US EXIT & FALL OF SAIGON
Paris Peace Accords (1973), NVA Spring Offensive & The Fall of Saigon (1972–75)
The Jan 1973 Paris Peace Accords withdrew US troops while leaving ~150,000 NVA soldiers inside South Vietnam, as Watergate and Congress ended US aid;
General Dung’s Mar–Apr 1975 Spring Offensive shattered ARVN from Ban Me Thuot and Da Nang to Saigon, ending two decades of US intervention (58,220 US dead).
